newsitem.title: USA: Compuserve trims loss in latest quarter.
newsitem.headline: Compuserve trims loss in latest quarter.

text.p: CompuServe Corp., whose chief executive resigned earlier this week, Thursday reported a fiscal third-quarter loss and said it would focus on returning to profitability as it cuts costs and realigns its business structure.
The world's No. 2 online service also reported a decline in membership in its flagship CSi service, but said there were improvements in membership in other areas.

CompuServe said it lost $14.2 million, or 15 cents a share, in its third quarter ended Jan. 31 vs. a profit of $17.2 million, or 13 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues rose to $211 million from $203 million.

"While our third-quarter results show improvement over the second quarter, they are clearly not good enough," said Frank Salizzoni, CompuServe's chairman and acting CEO. "Our No. 1 priority is to stabilise earnings and return to profitability as quickly as possible," he said in a statement accompanying the results.
In the Columbus, Ohio-based company's second quarter, it recorded a loss of $58 million, or 63 cents a share, including special charges, on $214 million in revenues.
Salizzoni is acting as CEO while the company seeks a replacement for Robert Massey, who resigned Monday.

CompuServe said subscribers to its flagship CSi online service were down at the end of the quarter by 100,000 to 2.8 million, with most of the decline coming from the U.S. market. Its U.S. subscribers dropped 140,000 to 1.6 million.
European subscribers grew to 873,000, up 54,000 from 819,000 in the second quarter. Subscribers from other overseas areas fell 14,000 to 365,000.
CompuServe said its Internet-only access service, Sprynet, grew to 270,000 members from 218,000 in the second quarter.

Members for the combined CSi online service and Sprynet totalled 3,162,000 in the third quarter, down from 3,312,000 in the second quarter. CompuServe's exit from its flat-rate Wow! service for consumers and families accounted for 102,000 of the 150,000-member decline in subscribers.
CompuServe's Japanese licensee, Nifty, grew to 2.17 million, from 2.02 million in the previous quarter.
Including Nifty, CompuServe's total subscribers remained flat at 5,341,000 in the third quarter, ranking the company second in the online industry behind America Online, which has 8 million members.
Monthly revenue per subscriber improved in the third quarter to $15.22, compared with $15.06 in the second quarter and $14.48 in the first quarter.
The troubled online service also said that it will continue to invest in its commercial networking business, which has been a successful source of growth.
In the third quarter, Network Services added 90 corporate customers, compared with 52 in the second quarter. CompuServe now has 1,151 customers for data communications and other corporate services.
CompuServe's stock rose 75 cents to $11.25 in early trading on Nasdaq.
